study_identification_part.si4_title: Lifespan development of thalamic nuclei and characterizing thalamic nuclei abnormalities in schizophrenia using normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states research objectives with explicit goals. The authors provide three specific aims: 1) characterize age effects on thalamic nuclei using normative models; 2) clarify the association between cognition and thalamic nuclei volumes across time; 3) apply normative models to determine the frequency of thalamic structure abnormalities in schizophrenia and examine if deviation scores were associated with cognitive impairment. The purpose of applying normative modeling is explicitly described (identifying individuals with abnormalities for precision medicine). Both criteria are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "With that in mind, the goals of this study are to: 1) characterize age effects on thalamic nuclei using normative models; 2) clarify the association between cognition and thalamic nuclei volumes, and determine how they change over time; and 3) apply our normative models of thalamic nuclei development to determine the frequency of thalamic structure abnormalities in an independent sample of individuals with schizophrenia and examine if deviation scores were associated with cognitive impairment." Also: "Identifying which individuals show abnormality is essential to unraveling the complex etiology of schizophrenia and precision medicine."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "GAMLSS models were fitted to thalamic nuclei volumes separately for each hemisphere to model nonlinear age effects (on the outcome mean and variance) over the lifespan (ranging 5-100), stratified by sex, race, intracranial volumes and included random intercepts for families" ... nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: This study builds a NEW normative model. The criterion requires a data partitioning strategy where the model is tested on samples not used for fitting. The study does not describe using a hold-out test set, K-fold cross-validation, or leave-one-out cross-validation for validating the normative model on the reference cohort. The model was built using the entire HCP Lifespan cohort and then applied to an independent clinical cohort, but no internal validation partition is described for the reference cohort itself.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No supporting text found describing internal validation through data partitioning of the reference cohort. nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: This study builds a NEW normative model. The criterion requires the normative model to be applied to an independent external dataset of healthy individuals not used for model development. The study applied the model to the healthy control group from the schizophrenia cohort (n=211) as an independent validation. They report that 85.3% of healthy individuals fell within the 90% range across thalamic subdivisions, indicating reasonable generalization. However, this validation is limited as the primary purpose was to compare with schizophrenia patients, not comprehensive external validation of the normative model itself.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "The validity of this model was tested using our healthy control group, and we identified the proportion of individuals who fell within 90% of the population. Across all thalamic subdivisions, a median of 85.3% of healthy individuals fell within the 90% range, indicating that the normative models generalized reasonably well to an independent sample."
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.location: Huang2024.pdf.md, Results section (Individual deviation from normative ranges in schizophrenia)

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: This study builds a NEW normative model. All criteria are satisfied: 1) Type of statistical model specified: GAMLSS (Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale, and Shape) is clearly specified. 2) Key model settings described: Natural cubic spline function with 2 equally-spaced knots, generalized gamma distribution, natural logarithm linkage for mu and sigma, identity linkage for nu, random intercepts for families. 3) Software and libraries specified: GAMLSS R package, neuroCombat R package, geepack R package Version 1.3.9, R Version 4.1.3.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "Normative modeling of thalamic nuclei change over the lifespan was conducted using generalized additive models for location, scale, and shape (GAMLSS); a robust and flexible framework for modeling nonlinear growth trajectories." From Supplemental Methods: "ns represents natural cubic spline function with 2 equally-spaced knots over the age range (5 to 100 years)... The natural logarithm linkage function was used for mu and sigma, and identify linkage function was used for nu." Software: "neuroCombat R package", "geepack R package Version 1.3.9", "R Version 4.1.3"

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "We computed individual centile scores for all individuals in our Schizophrenia Cohort to place each individual based on their distance from the median of the age-normed, sex, and race-stratified distributions provided by the reference sample" ... This classification provided individualized thalamus deviation maps in which each thalamus subdivision was numerically coded as 1 (supra-normal), 0 (normal), or -1 (infra-normal)." ... "we observed significant associations in the schizophrenia group using centile values but not the standardized raw volumes in the bilateral mediodorsal and pulvinar" ...
